clue.text: Brush suit before church

parts.note: to suit is to fit, as clothes do

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a suit with a brush before setting off for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' looks like a verb for grooming the suit; it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitch is a fine artist's or decorator's brush, originally made from polecat hair.

clue.text: Initially call to account for capital

parts.note: first means at the start, initially
to rate someone is to scold them

explanation.surface: A treasurer is first asked to explain where the money went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial; it means excellent. 'Initially' is not a first-letter signal here but gives FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is an old-fashioned word for excellent, top-notch.

clue.text: A river sailor seen around before midday

indicators.note: the sailor's word goes round the outside of the morning abbreviation

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A seaman is spotted near the water one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar forms most of the boundary between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is a river in the West Country flowing into Plymouth Sound.

clue.text: Pass several — so liberal

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
some means several, a number of

explanation.surface: Passing around several helpings shows generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' is not political but generous, as in a handsome reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean generous or ample, as in a handsome sum.

clue.text: Pays for changes?

definitions.meaning: to redress a wrong is to make amends or compensate for it
read as ..., puts clothes on again, i.e. changes outfit

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who pays when things are altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress means compensation for a wrong, while re-dressing means getting dressed again, a change of clothes.

clue.text: Pity the young widow staying with her mother-in-law!

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for compassion or sorrow

definitions.text: the young widow staying with her mother-in-law
definitions.meaning: the Old Testament widow who stayed with Naomi

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a bereaved young woman who stays loyal to her husband's family.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, the widowed Moabite refuses to leave her mother-in-law Naomi.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an old noun for compassion, surviving in ruthless; it is also the biblical heroine's name.

clue.text: Engaging heavyweight to appear in a Northern town

parts.note: darling as an adjective means charming, engaging
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A charming boxing heavyweight makes an appearance in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Darlington is a town in County Durham in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is a market town in north-east England, famous for its early railway.

clue.text: A woman in extremity — turned out

indicators.note: the woman's name sits inside the word for the extremity

parts.note: an end is an extremity
Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in dire straits is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' suggests evicted; it means happened as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed as a consequence, as things turned out.

clue.text: Food from Peg that is totally cooked

indicators.note: the whole phrase of letters is cooked, worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A dish made by Peg that is overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totally cooked' rearranges PEG THAT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a type of pasta, a staple food.

clue.text: European agreement over as yet unused power

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, on top of, the second

parts.note: si is yes in Italian and Spanish
new means not yet used

explanation.surface: A European treaty is concluded over a fresh source of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'finished'; in a down clue it places one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means muscular strength, as in the sinews of war.

clue.text: Seeing spirit in a mount, one speculates

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A drinker spots a bottle of spirits up on a hill and starts musing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' is only a link word, and 'in' looks like a container signal but simply stands for itself. A tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminator is someone who mulls things over, a thinker who ponders at length.

clue.text: Drive around a foreign country

indicators.note: the letters of 'drive' are wrapped around the single letter given by 'a'

parts.note: a drive in a car is a spin

explanation.surface: Someone takes a motoring holiday touring abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country in Europe, foreign from the British setter's point of view.

clue.text: Prematurely ended the career of a singer

indicators.note: the word 'the' is cut off before its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: A sports report on someone whose career was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prematurely ended' clips the word 'the' to TH; 'career' is the verb, to hurtle along, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, so it is a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: How to follow lots of players for a little extra entertainment

indicators.note: the word 'How' comes after the teams, following them in the answer

parts.note: sides are teams, groups of several players
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guide on how to keep track of a large cast, as a minor amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a minor attraction at a fair, a small additional diversion.

clue.text: Grants made once all was settled

indicators.note: letters that have been settled are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Funding is handed out once everything has been agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' rearranges ONCE ALL WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are sums granted or allotted regularly to someone.

clue.text: The company taking ages blames reorganisation

indicators.note: reorganising something rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A firm that is slow to restructure blames its sluggishness on the shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganisation' rearranges AGES and BLAMES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering of people, a company or collection.

clue.text: A good man to put down the latest news

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
to oppress is to put down or subjugate

explanation.surface: A virtuous person is asked to set down the newest headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop press was a late news column added to a newspaper after printing began.
explanation.definitionFit: A late item inserted in a paper after the presses have started counts as last-minute news.

clue.text: Leave it in some haste — that's the answer

indicators.note: the answer is found inside some of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An editor in a rush tells a typesetter what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some' picks the letters out of 'haste — that's'. Stet is the proofreader's mark meaning 'let it stand'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a Latin instruction to a printer meaning let the original stand, ignoring a correction.

clue.text: Though perhaps perfect at the top, head shows strain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above, at the top of, the second

parts.note: the perfect is one grammatical tense
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A boss, flawless at the top, shows signs of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is the grammatical tense, not flawless; a NESS is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenseness is a state of tension or strain.

clue.text: Rustic poems, possibly written in German

indicators.note: the rearranged verse is set down inside the word for a German

parts.note: Hun is a dated slang term for a German

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of poems may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Country verse, perhaps composed in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the verse word, and 'written in' sets that jumble inside a dated slang term for a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, like rough cloth woven at home.

clue.text: The Queen — very large and famous statue

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A guide describes the monarch and a huge, celebrated statue.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros is the popular name for the statue atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in London's Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure in Piccadilly Circus is widely known by the name of the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Moving, though quite mad, proposal

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A debate where a crazy motion is nonetheless touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like 'emotionally touching'; it means travel from place to place.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the act of travelling or going from place to place.

clue.text: Panic about cold, in short

indicators.note: the word for panic goes about, around, the abbreviation for cold

parts.note: a scare is a panic
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Alarm grows about a brief cold snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like 'briefly'; it means in short supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, hard to find.

clue.text: Remarkable pieces thrown by a beginner at wheel

indicators.note: pieces thrown about land in a jumbled order

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate, a beginner behind the wheel

explanation.surface: A novice potter at the wheel turns out remarkable pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges PIECES into ESPECI; a British learner driver displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or particular, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: A seed concoction was found soothing

definitions.note: a passive phrase standing for a past-tense verb meaning brought relief

indicators.note: a concoction mixes ingredients up, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy made from seeds proves calming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges A SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means relieved or calmed, as soothing something does.

clue.text: Majestic bearing to give delight

parts.note: regal means kingly, majestic
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A stately poise that pleases onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like deportment, going with 'Majestic'; it is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain or amuse them richly.

clue.text: Taking a drink about four is vital

indicators.note: the drink goes about, around, the Roman numeral

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Having a pint at around four o'clock is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' looks like 'essential'; it means full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital in its root sense means living, having life.

clue.text: Alarm's loud to attract attention

annotationWithheld.why: Alarm's loud to attract attention (4) for LEAR: no parse found giving LEAR from these words, and a search of the exact clue found nothing

clue.text: Absolute quiet always required

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A demand for total, permanent silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means utter or complete, as in sheer madness.

clue.text: Keen team formed in part of London

parts.note: keen prices are low, cheap ones
a side is a team

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic team is set up in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' is not enthusiastic but low-priced, as in keen prices. Cheapside is a street in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapside is a historic market street in the City, London's financial district.

clue.text: A pharmacist's coin-in-the-slot machine

definitions.meaning: a chemist who makes up and hands out prescribed medicines
a vending machine that gives out goods when paid

explanation.surface: A chemist's shop has a vending machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a chemist who makes up prescriptions and a vending machine give out goods, the shared sense of the word.

clue.text: The more of these people have the more they want!

definitions.text: The more of these people have the more they want!

parts.words: The more of these people have the more they want!
parts.note: a paradox: having more of them means wanting more, since they are wants by definition

explanation.surface: A wry saying about greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are requirements or wants, so having many of them means lacking much.
